item.research_question: How does dendritic liquation during casting influence the spatial formation of martensite crystals in TiZrHfCoNiCu versus CoNiCuAlGaIn high entropy shape memory alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting from high-purity elements (iodide Ti, Zr, Hf; electrolytic Co, Ni, Cu; Al, Ga, In) in pre-gettered argon; ingots turned and re-melted nine times; weight 5–10 g; DTA heating/cooling rates of 40 K min−1
item.test_conditions: Room temperature SEM imaging; DTA measurements with ±7K accuracy; EDX line scans across dendritic and interdendritic regions
key_findings: TiZrHfCoNiCu crystallization starts at 1530 K with a peak width of 120 K, while CoNiCuAlGaIn starts at 1500 K with a peak width of 174 K.
In Ti16.67Zr16.67Hf16.67Co10Ni25Cu15, martensite crystals fill the dendrites, whereas in Co31.22Ni29.26Cu11.95Al16.64Ga10.39In0.55, they form only in interdendritic regions.
The crystallization temperature for Ti16.67Zr16.67Hf16.67Co10Ni25Cu15 is 1250 K, with a peak width of 164 K, compared to 1587 K and 65 K for binary TiNi.
Martensite crystals in Co31.22Ni29.26Cu11.95Al16.64Ga10.39In0.55 stop at the boundary of dendrites, with a 20-μm long crystal staying entirely within the interdendritic region.
The correlation coefficient between enthalpy and entropy of mixing is −0.87 for TiZrHfCoNiCu, while for CoNiCuAlGaIn, enthalpy of mixing correlates with Cu concentration at 0.99.
Dendrite regions in TiZrHfCoNiCu show the highest entropy of mixing (14.61 Jmol−1K−1) and atomic size difference, correlating with martensite formation.
Interdendritic regions in TiZrHfCoNiCu are stabilized against martensitic transformation due to lower negative enthalpy of mixing and lower entropy of mixing.
item.mechanism: Martensite crystals form in regions with higher lattice distortion (higher atomic size difference and entropy of mixing) and propagate through these highly distorted areas but cannot penetrate less distorted regions where diffusional phase transformations (precipitation) stabilize the austenite phase.
item.limitations: Strong dendritic liquation leads to chemical inhomogeneities and precipitates (e.g., Ti2Ni-like phases) that degrade shape memory behavior upon fatigue; simple solution treatments cannot fully avoid these precipitations.
item.future_work: Control of crystallization parameters to refine microstructures for cast and ready-to-use HESMA without subsequent solutionizing, particularly for 3D printing applications.
quotes: In contrast, in the CoNiCuAlGaIn system the dendritic liquation allows the martensite crystals to form only in interdendritic regions.
The dendrites in Figure 3a appear brighter than the interdendritic regions, while in Figure 3b the situation is vice versa.
Martensite crystals are not able to penetrate the less distorted interdendritic regions that are also less stable.
